title: Control Spark Join Hash Partitioning
question:
I have three dataframes A, B, and C. I need to join dataframes A and B on columns [a, b] and dataframes A and C on columns [a, c].

I would like to force Spark to only hash-partition the three dataframes A, B, and C by the common column "a". Thereby, for the two joins I would need three hash-partitioning.

By doing so I would save one hash-partitioning: By default Spark is going to hash-partition A twice, by [a, b] in the first join and, afterwards, by [a, c] in the second join.

Is it possible to achieve such saving?

For example,

AB = A.join(B, ["a", "b"], "inner")
AC = A.join(C, ["a", "c"], "inner")
AB.explain()
AC.explain()

answer: Although, the plan shows hash partitioning of A twice for creating both the joined dataframes AB and AC, it does not mean under the hood the tasks are not reusing already hashed partitions of A . Spark skips the stages if it finds the steps redundant even if its part of the plan. Can you check your DAG to see if the stages are skipped like shown below?
